The season started on 24 January 2020{{cite web |url=https://redgol.cl/chile/ANFP-define-fechas-de-inicio-de-la-liguilla-de-Primera-B-y-el-Campeonato-Nacional-de-2020-en-Primera-Division-20191220-0065.html|title=ANFP define fechas de inicio de la liguilla de Primera B y el Campeonato Nacional de 2020 en Primera División|language=es|publisher=RedGol|date=20 December 2019|access-date=24 December 2019}} and ended on 17 February 2021 with the relegation play-off. [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]] were the defending champions, having won the [[2019 Chilean Primera División|previous tournament]]. They successfully defended their title, winning their fifteenth league championship and third in a row with a game to spare on 10 February 2021 after tying 0–0 at home with eventual league runners-up [[Unión La Calera]].{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/tricampeones-la-historia-se-rinde-ante-la-uc/YIFPT3OPF5C7DINV4BTSFHBVEQ/|title=Tricampeones: la historia se rinde ante la UC|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=10 February 2021}} The competition was suspended from 18 March to 29 August 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile|COVID-19 pandemic]]. ==Format changes== For this season, and given that the previous season was declared as concluded with no relegations to the [[Primera B de Chile|Primera B]], ANFP approved an expansion of the first tier to 18 teams, with two teams promoted from the second tier joining the 16 teams that competed in the top flight in 2019. The 18 teams played each other twice (once at home and once away) for a total of 34 matches. Qualification for the [[2020 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] and [[2020 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] was awarded to the top eight teams at the end of the season.{{cite web|url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2019/12/07/futbol/1575678270_726277.html|title=Así será el formato del torneo de Primera y la B en 2020|publisher=AS Chile|language=es|date=6 December 2019|access-date=24 December 2019}} Originally, the [[2020 Copa Chile|Copa Chile]] champions would have been the fourth qualifier for the Copa Libertadores but since the 2020 Copa Chile would not be held before the start of the Copa Libertadores qualifying stages, its allocated berth was awarded to the fourth-placed team of the Campeonato Nacional instead.{{cite web|url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/12/31/futbol/1609370744_438287.html|title=Consejo de la ANFP modificó las bases para los cupos de Libertadores y Sudamericana|publisher=AS Chile|language=es|date=30 December 2020|access-date=11 February 2021}} Since there were no relegated teams in the previous season, in this season three teams were relegated to the second tier: the last-placed team in the standings of the 2020 season, the last-placed team in a relegation table which was elaborated considering the performance in both the 2019 and 2020 seasons, and the losers of a play-off between the teams placed second-to-last of both tables.{{cite web|url=https://www.publimetro.cl/cl/grafico-chile/2019/12/20/bases-campeonato-nacional-2020.html|title=Tres descensos y más de 2 (ANFP) announced the suspension of the Campeonato Nacional as well as the rest of its tournaments due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile|COVID-19 pandemic]], starting from 18 March 2020.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/la-tercera-pm/noticia/la-anfp-suspende-el-futbol-a-causa-del-coronavirus/43ODKTMASNGIDBNID5NRHQ65MY/|title=Se suspende el campeonato: la ANFP extrema medidas por el coronavirus|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=16 March 2020}} On 8 June, ANFP's Council of Presidents decided to resume the league on 31 July with matches to be played behind closed doors and clubs having at least four weeks of training sessions, pending approval from the Chilean government.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/los-clubes-aprueban-que-e-futbol-profesional-vuelva-el-31-de-julio/XXQACN6WQJB6DM42WVF7A2DKN4/|title=Los clubes chilenos aprueban que el fútbol profesional vuelva el 31 de julio|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=8 June 2020}} However, this original date had to be pushed back as clubs were only given approval to resume training sessions starting from 16 July, with the ANFP considering the weekend of 8 August as a new tentative date of resumption, following three weeks of training sessions.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/la-tercera-pm/noticia/cuando-es-el-pitazo-inicial-en-el-futbol-chileno-las-fechas-y-obligaciones-que-siguen-al-retorno-a-los-entrenamientos/CZZVR55H3FD5ZHE4MDUQ6NKDQA/|title=¿Cuándo es el pitazo inicial en el fútbol chileno? Las fechas y obligaciones que siguen al retorno a los entrenamientos|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=13 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020}} On 19 August, in a press conference held at [[Estadio Nacional Julio Martínez Prádanos]] in Santiago, Chilean President [[Sebastián Piñera]] confirmed 29 August as the date of resumption of both the first and second tier seasons, with games to be played behind closed doors. The first matches to be played would be the ones postponed from previous rounds, while the ninth round of the Campeonato Nacional would be played on the weekend of 4–6 September.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/pinera-anuncia-el-regreso-del-futbol-para-el-sabado-29-de-agosto/UXGQPWFNZRE6HGF65ACGDKXD2E/|title=Piñera anuncia el regreso del fútbol para el sábado 29 de agosto|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=19 August 2020|access-date=21 August 2020}} On 26 September the match between [[Colo-Colo]] and [[C.D. Antofagasta|Deportes Antofagasta]], scheduled to be played on that day at 11:00, was suspended due to the discovery of a positive COVID-19 case in the former team following their return from Brazil where they played a [[2020 Copa Libertadores group stage#C3 v C2|Copa Libertadores group stage match]] against [[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico Paranaense]].{{cite web |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Deportes/2020/09/26/999044/Se-suspende-Colo-Colo-Antofagasta.html|title=No se juega: Se suspende Colo Colo-Antofagasta por un caso de covid en los albos|language=es|publisher=Emol.com|date=26 September 2020}} It was eventually rescheduled for 10 November at 11:00, with Colo-Colo fined for the postponement of the match as well as the delay to submit their PCR test results prior to said match.{{cite web |url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/11/06/futbol/1604623131_267449.html|title=ANFP reprogramó duelo entre Colo Colo y Antofagasta|language=es|publisher=AS Chile|date=5 November 2020|access-date=8 November 2020}} On 11 December, the ANFP announced the suspension of the Round 23 matches between [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] and [[Deportes Iquique]] and between [[Unión La Calera]] and [[O'Higgins F.C.|O'Higgins]] due to positive cases for COVID-19 being reported in Deportes Iquique and Unión La Calera.{{cite web |url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/12/12/futbol/1607731872_493275.html|title=El fútbol chileno sufre con el Covid: dos partidos suspendidos|language=es|publisher=AS
